rendered:
The premise does not hold: the document does not say bare Al outperformed carbon/Al at 4 mA/cm^2[1]. At that current the carbon/Al electrode showed a voltage hysteresis of 45 mV[2]. For bare Al the document says the opposite: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents[3]. Its failure mode was shorting: the bare Al electrode exhibits signs of shorting[4], which the authors attribute to uneven plating that occurs due to the higher[5] nucleation overpotential. By contrast, the carbon/Al electrodes demonstrate more stable plating and stripping with higher[6] Coulombic efficiency. The carbon layer lowers the nucleation overpotential, reported as 19 to 12 mV[7], which the authors give as the mechanism for the better behavior.

So the document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at 4 mA/cm^2[8], and therefore no figure for how much lower bare Al's hysteresis was. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is to earlier work using Cu electrodes, which the authors say reported nearly double the hysteresis at[9] 4 mA/cm^2[10] (a comparison shown in their Figure S4). That is a different system from bare Al in this work, so it should not be read as bare Al's hysteresis.
